sermon.title: Leadership in the Last Days
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer studies Isaiah 3 and 4 to explain why God removes designated leaders, saying unqualified leadership, role reversal in the home, and giving in to money, popularity and sexual temptation lead the church into error. He argues for Jesus as Lord over all leaders, discusses his views on conservative politics and fundamentalism, and says the word and Spirit must burn sin out of the church.

Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: he says “Jesus said in Psalms” for the words about God giving them their desire but sending leanness to their soul, which are in Psalm 106:15. Several caption slips are corrected where the word is clear (for example “ss” to “sows”), and four spots are marked [unclear] (“a se thing,” a church name, “inra waving,” and a word in “when I wasn’t…”). He names public figures and organizations (a senator, a news network, and three well-known preachers) in his remarks; those names stay in the transcript only. His statements about women leaders, race, political parties, statistics, and other Christian groups are his own opinions and are not verified here.

chunks.section_question: How do the word and the Holy Spirit burn sin out of us? (Jeremiah 31:33, Luke 24:32, Jeremiah 23:28)
chunks.short_answer: He says the “spirit of judgment and the spirit of burning” (Isaiah 4:4) is God’s word and Spirit coming to us and burning things out of us, as he experienced, changing his thinking and desires “little by little.” He says he does not need psychology but a meeting with God, and that Scripture is a fire and a hammer, so we should read the Bible, since friends “they’ll agree you’re okay.”
chunks.text:
And so he will come and he will burn it out of you. And that’s what I experienced back there and at a [unclear] church, coming up every Sunday, letting God deal with something in my life. I didn’t know this word, but it was working. He would come to me and he would change my thinking, he would change my desires, little by little, step by step. He kept changing me by the word and the spirit coming to me. That’s the magical cure, the word and the Holy Spirit. Are you out there, church? That’s why prayer is important. That’s why alter calls are important. That’s why a real worship service in spirit and truth is important. It’s that time when God can burn. He’s either burning something out or he’s [unclear] burning something in. And that what he says in the new covenant: “I will inscribe my word in your minds and heart.” He’s either burning something in, the Ten Commandments was written by the finger of God, burnt right into the stone, or he’s burning something out. Wow. And so, see, I don’t need psychology, I don’t need human intellect, I need a meeting with God where he transforms my life supernaturally by the burning of his spirit and the burning of his word. And I experienced all that. I didn’t know all this stuff when I was experiencing. You don’t have to know it to experience it, but knowing it really expedites it, speeds up the experience, doesn’t it? I mean, I could have grew a lot faster if I had known what you people know.

Luke 24:32: did not “Did not our heart burn within us while Jesus talked with us by the way, and while he open to us the scriptures?” Do the scriptures do that to you? Do they burn in you? Do they get opened? Or you just reading through your Bible, you’re not even reading it? Why do I push people to read their Bible? Because the Bible will burn things in you and burn things out of you. At my lowest time in my Christian walk, I never failed to read the Bible, and the scripture would bring me back to the middle of the road every time. You can’t trust your friends. They’ll agree you’re okay. I don’t need somebody telling me I’m okay when I’m not not okay. I need the Bible, who is impartial, just bucking me, telling me to buck up. How about you? chunks.section_question: What is God’s glory over His church, and how should we respond? (Jeremiah 23:29, Isaiah 4:5-6, Matthew 16:18, Romans 8:26)
chunks.short_answer: He says Isaiah 4:5-6 promises “a cloud by day and a fire by night,” the glory of God as “the demonstration of his power” in the church, with gifts such as wisdom, knowledge, prophecy, tongues, healing and miracles, and a tabernacle for shade and shelter. He says we should get away from “the mighty man of God mentality,” pray “here I am, use me,” and let Christ burn in us and out of us, as he did in his own life.
chunks.text:
Now we know that in most cases the chaff is the wicked people that is burned in that last day in the lake of fire. Okay, but also in the Bible the chaff is that worthless part of the wheat, that sinful, that old sinful nature of man, that old man, that chaff. And he says, “What is the chaff to the wheat? Is not my word like a fire that will burn that chaff out of you? Is not my word like a hammer?” If you’re hard and stubborn, that word will come along and keep chipping away until there is something beautiful formed in your life. Amen. How many could use a little hammering? Yeah, some of us are hard-headed. It takes the hammer. And uh, I needed both the fire and the hammer. I was hard-headed, and I needed things burned out of my life. Isn’t that beautiful? And see, Isaiah said all this thousands of years before our day, and this is what I like: tremendous promise. And I’m trying to get this church to rise up to this truth.

Okay, after I get these things dealt with in my life, then the Lord, who’s going to do it? The Lord. Not Olstein, not Rick Warren, not Joy Meyers. The Lord is going to do this. All right, not Dave Kincer, by the way. “The Lord will create above every dwelling place of Mount Zion.” Okay, Mount Zion is the church. The dwelling places are the assemblies, the local churches like us. Every dwelling place in Zion, above her assemblies, “a cloud by day and a fire by night.” See, I told told you, and and he goes on to say, “for over all the glory there will be a covering.” I told you that the glory of God in the Bible was the demonstration of his power, where it was a cloud or a fire, parting the Red Sea, healing the sick, saving a soul. It was the glory. It was the demonstration of the power of his presence. And this is what Isaiah is saying, church. If you’ll let me burn in you you and burn things out of you, I will demonstrate myself in your midst. You will have a word of wisdom, a word of knowledge, a prophecy, a tongue, an interpretation, healing, miracles, discerning of spirits and faith. They will be active in your church, because that is the demonstration of my glory.

Do the church need that? Yeah. Do Christians need the demonstration? Yes. Somebody’s got to push into this, folks. Now, we can talk about the things of God till we’re dead, but we need to enter into the things of God. God said he would do it. Like in prayer at the end, “Let there be a performance, Lord. You said Now put up.” Amen. See, do we really care about our nation, to seek God for his glory? Because his glory is going to turn this nation around, I guarantee you. You got to be really hard to reject Christ in that day, and a lot of the people on the fence, a lot of the lukewarm, are going to come over to the right side. Hallelujah. Then he goes on to say, “There will be a tabernacle for shade Allelujah in the daytime from the heat,” and there’s going to be a tabernacle for a refuge, a place of protection, a stronghold, and there’s going to be a tabernacle for a shelter from storms and the rain. The wise man built his house upon the rocks. When the storms came, the problems of life, the troubles of life came, he stood. Now folks, I don’t know about you, but it’s worth letting Christ burn out of me and burn in me to get these kind of results.

And we got to get away from the mighty man of God mentality. God is building a church that the gates of hell should not prevail against. God is building a glorious church, church without spot or wrinkle, at think not some mighty man of God. And so when the church will press in, God will demonstrate, because when the church presses in, the streams the part they have flow out and makes a big river, and things get done. Are you with me? No, all of us won’t prophesy. The Bible says that all of us won’t speak in tongues, all of us won’t interpret, but there’ll be enough of us till we get the job done. Boy, I like that. There’s not enough of us now saying, “Here I am, Lord, use me.” That was what the Holy Ghost revealed to me this morning in prayer. They need to be praying, “Here I am, use me,” not telling me what I already know. They need to say, “Lord, use me. Here I am. There’s homes out there. Here I am, commission me, send me, equip me.” Are you there? You got to bring prayer down to your personal reaction. Anybody can pray about something, and anybody can wait for the pastor to do everything. That’s what we’ve been doing for decades in America, and it hasn’t worked, has it?

But the real Christian will sayl, “Here I am, use me, use my prayers, use my worship, use my prayer, use my fasting through the week. Use me, Lord, if nothing else to ignite the one that can prophesy.” Amen. One of the young people came up to me this morning and said, “Were you speaking in tongues in prayer?” And I said, “Yes, I was.” I said it’s rare these days. I’ve only spoken in tongues about three times in the last year, and it used to be very steadily. And I was explaining to them how you can speak in tongues and you can interpret it and you can know what the Holy Spirit’s saying. See, the Bible says we don’t know how to pray as we ought, but the spirit does. See, and the Bible says pray in the spirit and sing in the spirit, isn’t that right? So we got to make that transition to the spirit. Hallelujah. I thought I was speaking low enough to were no one heard me, but they were nailing me, and they said they really help them. I said good, because in it’s real, it really ministers. When it’s not real, it’s just in the way. When we’re pantomiming, pretending to speak in tongues, it there’s nothing there. Amen.

Church, so are we going to be this glorious church, this church at the gates of hell cannot prevail against? Let Christ burn in us and burn out of us. How many, you raise your hands and “Lord, bring me the burning”? Yes. See that, and that makes it, that makes it for me as a young Christian, when the Holy Spirit revealed these things to me, it really got me relaxed. God’s going to work in me. I I I can’t just grip my teeth and make this happen. God’s going to do this, and that just brought a peace on my life, and he did, he slowly got me there. I had to learn to like myself when I wasn’t [unclear]. I wanted to run, because, you know, the Lord shows light on you and you see yourself and, oh God, what there’s no hope, I’m still doing that same stupid thing I was doing two weeks ago when I asked God to deliver me from it. But see, when you know that you have done what God said to do, repent, admit it, and let God work, then you’re at peace, because you know he’s going to keep his word and get the job done. Hallelujah. Then I could live with myself, I could accept myself, and God used me while he was working on me. I led a lot of people to Christ while he was leading me to Christ. Amen, church.

then the LORD will create above every dwelling place of Mount Zion, and above her assemblies, a cloud and smoke by day and the shining of a flaming fire by night. For over all the glory there will be a covering.

faqs.question: What does he say Jerusalem, Judea and Zion stand for?
faqs.answer: He says that Jerusalem, Judea and Zion are used “to teach us in these latter days the church,” so Isaiah 3 is about the church and not the heathen.

scriptures.text_nkjv: For behold, the Lord, the LORD of hosts, Takes away from Jerusalem and from Judah The stock and the store, The whole supply of bread and the whole supply of water;

faqs.question: What does he say causes the church to stumble?
faqs.answer: He says one source, the one Isaiah deals with, is “unqualified leadership,” and that it “may be okay for the crowd” to approve of things that are against God but “it doesn’t matter if they approve.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: For Jerusalem stumbled, And Judah is fallen, Because their tongue and their doings Are against the LORD, To provoke the eyes of His glory.

faqs.question: What is the difference between “babies” and “children” in Christ?
faqs.answer: He says babies know the Lord and are saved by the blood but have problems with sin, and children are learning and obeying but have not conquered Satan or become strong in the scriptures yet.

scriptures.text_nkjv: for you are still carnal. For where there are envy, strife, and divisions among you, are you not carnal and behaving like mere men?

faqs.question: What does he say about home Bible studies?
faqs.answer: He says when he investigated them “it’s just a bunch of babies and children Christians trying to teach babies and Christian children.”

faqs.question: Who does he say should lead the home?
faqs.answer: He says children should not lead the home, parents should, “and specifically the father,” who has directly from God the responsibility to provide food, clothing, shelter and medical care for his wife.

faqs.question: Does he say women can be leaders?
faqs.answer: He says “in the Bible, women can be rulers, but they are a small percent,” and that God chooses few women; he says it is wrong both to be against women leaders and to think just being a woman qualifies you.

faqs.question: What does he say a church leader must not do?
faqs.answer: He says a church leader cannot give people what they want, because “you’re only allowed to preach what the Bible says to preach,” even if people do not like it.

faqs.question: Does he say leadership depends on race, gender or age?
faqs.answer: He says no: it is “not the color of your skin… not whether you’re male or female… young or old… a college degree,” but “what you’ve experienced… the wisdom from above.”

faqs.question: What does he say about politics and the Bible?
faqs.answer: He says it is “a big lie that the American church has believed” that the Bible cannot be used for civil matters, since government, family and economics are all Bible topics and his word “is spirit.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: It is the Spirit who gives life; the flesh profits nothing. The words that I speak to you are spirit, and they are life.

faqs.question: What is the difference between praying “about” and praying “with compassion”?
faqs.answer: He says praying about something is different from “praying with compassion because you care,” and singing “about the Holy Spirit” is different from singing “by the Holy Spirit.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: What is the conclusion then? I will pray with the spirit, and I will also pray with the understanding. I will sing with the spirit, and I will also sing with the understanding.

faqs.question: What does he say about “once saved always saved”?
faqs.answer: He says it is “just wrong” and that it “taken repentance, turning from sin, right out,” and likewise says that the idea that water baptism is only symbolic is “the most ridiculous lie.”

faqs.question: What does he say it means to make Jesus Lord?
faqs.answer: He says “when you do what he says, that makes him your Lord,” and that when you only say “Jesus is my Lord and Savior” without doing it, “he’s not your Lord.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: “But why do you call Me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and not do the things which I say?

faqs.question: What does he say a wife should do if her husband asks her to violate the Bible?
faqs.answer: He says “your Lord Jesus is your number one leader,” and when a husband asks you to violate the lordship of Jesus, “you’re supposed to do what’s right.”

faqs.question: What does he say about raising his hands when he was first saved?
faqs.answer: He says he was “bashful and timid” and raising his hands “was a killer” because he thought everybody was watching, but he had the message to “repent and do what’s right.”

faqs.question: What does he say about speaking in tongues and being real?
faqs.answer: He says he speaks in tongues only about three times a year now, that tongues and interpretation can show what the Holy Spirit is saying, and that when it is not real, “it’s just in the way.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Likewise the Spirit also helps in our weaknesses. For we do not know what we should pray for as we ought, but the Spirit Himself makes intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.
